maxim: all things are lawful to those that are in Jack Feist
what: FRAMES AND MEMBERSHIPS — the arrangements under which identities take positions, and the positions they take.
why: An edge says A stands in relation R to B. A membership says A occupies position P inside grouping G. A frame says that under arrangement F, the memberships take THIS configuration. The archive needed the third because its own primary set does not have a single stable configuration: 'which figure stands outside the twelve rotates by frame.' Recording the Dodecad as one integer per identity — which is what the graph join did on 2026-09-09 before this file existed — flattens exactly the structure that makes it interesting.
the_case: Jack Feist occupies position 12 in the archive-default frame AND stands outside the twelve as *LOGOS, 'the closing position that closes by being the one that names.' Not either. Both. A scalar slot cannot say that; a membership with a topology can. Nobel Glas held the outside in the September 2025 Logotic Science frame and is canonicalised inside at position 10 in v1.1 — the same identity, two frames, two topologies.
